catalog_quote: Two- and three-syllable underived words are stressed on the first syllable, as shown in the next examples ... Four-syllable underived words receive secondary stress on the first syllable and main stress on the third syllable ... Words derived by reduplication retain main stress on the base of the word in accordance with the stress pattern in 3.4.1 above. ... Likewise, in nominalised words derived by means of the affix (-)in- (infixed or prefixed) stress remains on the root of the word ... Words formed by means of the noun-deriving suffix -ana are always stressed on the first syllable of the suffix ... A regular stress shift occurs when a verb becomes transitive. The main stress shifts to the vowel immediately preceding the object marker: /hápu/ 'cover' /hapú-a/ 'cover-it' /hapu-í-ɣɔ/ 'cover-TR-you' ...
